input.question: Just how different are the male and female brain?
input.ground_truth: There was a [thread](_URL_0_) earlier today in /r/AskScienceDiscussion about the brains of transgender men and women. You should give it a look, it has some interesting results about gender and brain morphology. It turns out the brains of transgender men and women most closely resemble the brains of the gender they identify with, not the sex they were born with. It also has some links to some of the primary literature about the sex differences in brain morphology. Should give you a good idea about how different the brains of men and women are.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Just how different are the male and female brain?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your brain is like a big toy box. Boys and girls both have toy boxes that are very similar — they have almost all the same toys inside. But sometimes, a few toys are arranged a little bit differently.

For example, on average, some parts of a boy’s brain might be a tiny bit bigger in some places, and some parts of a girl’s brain might be a little bit bigger in other places. But that doesn’t mean one brain is better or smarter — they’re just shaped a little differently, like how some kids have bigger shoes and some have smaller shoes.

Also, some studies say that on average, boys’ brains might be a bit more connected in certain areas, and girls’ brains might be more connected in other areas. But every brain is special and different, even between boys and girls who are friends!

So, the main thing is: our brains are a lot alike, but a few tiny pieces might look or work a little differently — kind of like how you and your friend might both have a red toy car, but yours has a sticker on it and your friend’s doesn’t.
